September 6, 1939.
Afternoon Translation

TA MEI WAN PAO'S OPEN LETTER TO WANG CHING-WEI

A letter dated September 2 sent by
Ling Pah-sen ( 林柏生 ), an adherent of Wang Ching-wei,
to the Chinese and English editions of the Ta Mei Wan Pao,
was published in the paper with the following Editorial note
on September 5 :-
We refute the allegation that the late
Mr. Chu Sing-kung ( 朱惺公 ) was a Communist. Such
allegations in the Far East have been incorrectly used as
a means to attack others, just as the expression "member
of the Bolshevik Party" is being commonly used in the
United States. We are opposed to all forms of terrorism,
no matter which party is responsible for their instigation.
We thank Mr. Ling for his kindness, but we still insist
that Mr. Wang Ching-wei alone is the proper person to
reply to this paper.

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.

SEP 5 - 1939

A Fair Offer
ON PAGE 1 of Saturday's Shanghai Evening Post, and in our Chinese edition Ta Mei Wan Pao, as well as in Sunday's Mercury and its Chinese edition Ta Mei Chou Pao, we made a fair offer to Mr. Wang Ching-wei. If he cares to receive the Editor of this newspaper and disclaim his present implied partnership with the murderous gangsters who—among other things—last Wednesday killed a valued member of our organization, we will deal with him fairly and see to it that he receives full accurate quotation both in Shanghai, and abroad. If he chooses to ignore our suggestion he pleads guilty to a charge we'd not care to have lie against us under any circumstances, and particularly not if we were trying to assume a position of public leadership.
We made the offer in good faith as is proved to a considerable extent, we believe, by the fact that the Editor asks no companion, bodyguard, or advance information as to where he is going. He will carry no weapons or protection aside from that pen which is reputedly more potent than the sword but which has never been considered the full equivalent of a bullet-proof vest. Our pledge is given that there will be accurate reporting of whatever Mr. Wang cares to impart. Our sole condition is that we want to see Mr. Wang direct, and that is for the sole reason that we want to be able to guarantee his statement as really coming from him.
It's up to Mr. Wang Ching-wei. He has been put in a most unenviable spot by the threats and violence of persons professing to be attached to him. If he can and will clear himself, here is his chance. If he lets our offer go unnoticed, we and the general public must enter against him a default judgment.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》

1939年9月5日

一项公平的提议

在周六的《上海晚邮报》第1版，以及我们的中文版《大美晚报》，还有周日的《水星报》及其中文版《大美周报》上，我们向汪精卫先生提出了一项公平的提议。如果他愿意接见本报编辑，并否认他目前与那伙谋杀暴徒之间心照不宣的合伙关系——这伙暴徒除其他罪行外，于上周三杀害了我们组织中的一位宝贵成员——我们将公平对待他，并确保他在上海及海外获得的引用准确无误。如果他选择无视我们的建议，他就等于承认了一项我们绝不愿在任何情况下背负的罪名，尤其是当我们试图承担公众领导地位时更是如此。
我们是本着诚意提出这一提议的，我们认为，编辑不要求任何同伴、保镖或事先告知去向，这在很大程度上证明了这一点。除了那支据说比剑更有力、但从未被视为防弹衣完全替代品的笔之外，他不会携带任何武器或防护措施。我们保证，无论汪先生愿意透露什么，都将得到准确报道。我们唯一的条件是我们要直接见到汪先生，这 solely 是因为我们要能够保证他的声明确实出自他本人之口。
这取决于汪精卫先生。那些声称依附于他的人所发出的威胁和暴力行为，已将他置于一个极令人羡慕的境地（注：原文 unenviable 意为令人羡慕的反面，即糟糕的、难堪的境地）。如果他能并且愿意澄清自己，这就是他的机会。如果他对我们的提议置之不理，我们和广大公众必须对他作出缺席判决。

Tea-Party To Press
By Wang Ching-wei
Still In Preparation
Preparations are being made for
the projected tea-party to be
given by Mr. Wang Ching-wei for
foreign correspondents in Shang-

has been informed by telephone
by Mr. Sih, liaison officer for Mr.
Wang and head of an office at
Room 405, 167 Avenue Edward
VII—the Shanghai Times Build-
ing.

article appearing in the Post
last Thursday on the ground that
the "mystery" alleged to surround
the reception, and his office, isn't
mysterious at all. The office is
registered duly with the police
authorities, he said, and the tea-
party hasn't been heard of lately
because preparations and the
guest-list aren't yet fully com-
pleted.
As to Mr. S.W. Li, with whom

been ill for several days but he
will soon be around again.

Open Letter to Mr. Wang Ching

American Editor and make clear
whether he sponsors such terro-
rism as caused the assassination

Chinese edition Ta Mei Wan Pao
last week, a letter from Mr. P.S

News appears today on the

enterprises, from which he more

intimation of a direct interview

be authorised.

汪精卫拟举行记者茶话会
仍在筹备中

据汪精卫先生的联络官、位于爱多亚路167号（《字林西报》大楼）405室办事处负责人施先生电话告知《上海晚邮报》，汪精卫先生计划为在上海的外国记者举行茶话会，目前正在进行筹备工作。
施先生对上周四《晚邮报》刊登的一篇文章表示轻微抗议，理由是所谓围绕接待活动及其办事处的“神秘色彩”根本不存在。他说，该办事处已在警察当局正式注册，而最近未闻茶话会之事，是因为筹备工作和宾客名单尚未完全确定。
关于《晚邮报》记者试图联系的李S.W.先生，施先生说他已经病了几天，但很快就会恢复工作。
至于《晚邮报》致汪精卫先生的公开信，要求其接见美方编辑并澄清是否赞助导致《大美晚报》一名职员上周遇刺的恐怖主义行为，今天社论版刊登了一封来自《华中日报》林P.S.先生的信。
林先生说，“汪先生对此案一无所知……你说得对，汪先生不可能与恐怖活动有任何牵连，他自己正是这些活动的受害者，且受害程度超过任何人……”但尽管所称声明据称已获授权，却并未暗示将安排与汪先生本人的直接会面。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
SEP 5 - 1939
24617
Terrorism

To the Editor:
Your letter of August 31, addressed to Mr. S.W. Li and Mr. Sih, (previous to and similar in sense to the September 2 Open Letter to Mr. Wang Ching-wei--EDITOR) has been forwarded, and I have been instructed, with reference to your request for a statement, to state the following:—
Mr. Wang Ching-wei knows nothing about the case nor about the person of Mr. Chu except that from his writings he is generally known to be a Communistic writer using his position in a foreign-owned publication to attack the true interests of China and spread subversive propaganda to which Mr. Wang however does not attach the slightest importance, although he is quite surprised that publications of your standing should break the rule that foreigners or Chinese employed by foreigners must maintain a strictly neutral and impartial attitude and not meddle in the internal politics of a country.
The point however is that political terrorism has originated with the Chungking authorities who have employed this inhuman and uncivilized weapon most extensively during recent months to do away with its political opponents. I was the first victim of their most dastardly attack. The second was Dr. Tseng Chung-ming who was killed, while Mr. Wang had a narrow escape; the assassins were, according to the investigations of the French authorities under the direct orders of the Chungking Secret Service, and several of them carried passports issued in Hongkong under the recommendation of a high official in the Southwest Transportation Company which is the main center of the Chungking Secret Service. Then followed Mr. Shen Tseh-kao who was dastardly killed only a few days ago. The instances which took place in Shanghai are too many to enumerate. But no word of condemnation ever came from the publications under your control although I find it hard to believe that you are condoning these dastardly acts of the Chungking authorities. Your editors are not the only ones who have received threatening letters. I myself, and every editor of the Central China Daily News in Shanghai and the South China Daily News in Hongkong are under constant threat to their lives. We denounced terrorism as a method of political warfare, but your publications kept silent. And this terrorism started by Chungking has led to all kinds of complications and encouraged common criminals and agents provocateurs in their nefarious activities.
It is needless to say that you were right in saying that Mr. Wang could not have anything to do with the terroristic enterprises from which he more than anybody else has himself suffered, but should you decide to make use of this letter in any way, I request that the letter be published in full.
Yours truly,
P.B. LIN,
Central China Daily News
Shanghai, Sept. 3, 1939.

恐怖主义

致编辑：
您8月31日致李S.W.先生和施先生的信（此前已发出，且与9月2日致汪精卫先生的公开信意思相似——编者注）已转交，奉命就您要求发表声明一事，陈述如下：——
汪精卫先生对此案及朱先生其人一无所知，仅从其文章得知，他一般被认为是一名共产主义作家，利用其在外国人办的出版物中的职位攻击中国的真正利益，散布颠覆性宣传，汪先生对此虽毫不重视，但对像贵报这样有地位的出版物竟打破外国人或受雇于外国人的中国人必须保持严格中立和公正态度、不干涉他国内政的规则，感到相当惊讶。
然而，关键在于，政治恐怖主义起源于重庆当局，他们在最近几个月广泛使用这种不人道和不文明的武器来消灭其政治对手。我是他们最卑鄙攻击的第一个受害者。第二个是曾仲明博士，他遇害身亡，而汪先生则幸免于难；根据法国当局的调查，刺客是在重庆特务处的直接命令下行事的，其中几人持有由西南运输公司（重庆特务处的主要中心）一位高官推荐而在香港签发的护照。随后是沈泽高先生，他在几天前也被卑鄙地杀害。发生在上海的此类事件不胜枚举。但是，在您控制的出版物中从未出现过谴责之言，虽然我很难相信您是在纵容重庆当局的这些卑鄙行径。收到恐吓信的并非只有您的编辑。我自己，以及上海《华中日报》和香港《华南日报》的每一位编辑，生命都受到持续威胁。我们谴责将恐怖主义作为政治战的手段，但您的出版物却保持沉默。而这种由重庆发起的恐怖主义导致了各种复杂局面，并鼓励了普通罪犯和挑衅代理人从事其邪恶活动。
不用说，您说得对，汪先生不可能与恐怖企业有任何关系，他自己正是这些活动的受害者，且受害程度超过任何人，但如果您决定以任何方式使用此信，我要求全文刊登该信。
此致，
林P.B.，
《华中日报》
上海，1939年9月3日。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.
AUG 31 1939
Another Journalist
Killed by Gunman
Mobile Police Patrol
Arrests Murderer ; Link
Seen with Other Crimes

Mr. Chu Sing-kung, columnist of the "Ta Mei Wan Pao" was shot and killed at 4.12 p.m. yesterday as he was walking down North Honan Road. His murderer was arrested a few seconds after he had perpetrated the crime, when a mobile police patrol passed in a motorcar and was able to prevent his escape.
Chu had just crossed N. Honan Road Bridge, coming from his office and was about to go home when suddenly, in front of the Embankment Building, a lone gunman advanced, fired a shot which entered the victim's right temple, and after throwing away his weapon, tried to make his escape by running northward along N. Honan Road. At this moment, the police car which was cruising near by, arrived at the scene, taking up the chase after the gunman who, seeing that no chance for an escape was left, gave himself up. He was taken to West Hongkew Police Station and after being questioned, was transferred to Chengtu Road Station as inquiries will be made in that district.

Motive Unknown
The reason for the murder is still puzzling the police, as Chu was known not to have had any political affiliations although, it was pointed out in Chinese circles last night, he frequently published anti-Wang Ching-wei articles which were sent him by readers.

Political Motive Suspected
The fact that detectives from Crime Branch Headquarters and the Special Branch were also investigating the case, indicated that a political motive may have been behind the murder but no definite confirmation on the subject could be obtained.
The weapon used by the gunman was a revolver which indicates that yesterday's assassination may have some connection with the shooting of Mr. Wang Chi-lu, another newspaperman, who, it will be recalled, was shot when he left his Rue Lafayette home on the morning of August 26 when, according to the French police revolvers were also used although, at the time, none of the gunmen was arrested.
The fact that the murder of Mr. Chu has been transferred to Chengtu Road Station may be an indication that he will be taken over to the French police for questioning, as it is well known that in most cases when the Settlement and the Concession police forces co-operate, this is done through Chengtu Road Station. On the other hand his transfer may have been merely made in order to facilitate the detectives' work.
A reliable though unofficial report had it last night that the murderer arrested yesterday declared that he was a guerilla. Should this be true and confirmed, the murder becomes all the more puzzling as the policy of the "Ta Mei Wan Pao" is pro-Chinese. On the other hand, if the murderer had some connection with the French Concession shooting affair, this may be correct because at the time, it was reported that Mr. Wang's paper had published advertisements for the Japanese-sponsored fish market in Hongkew.
Chu was reported to have received a number of threatening letters in the past, the last one on Tuesday.
Investigations are proceeding.

1939年8月31日
另一名记者
遭枪手杀害
流动巡逻警队
逮捕凶手；疑与其他犯罪有关联

《大美晚报》专栏作家朱惺公先生于昨日下午4时12分在河南北路行走时被枪杀。凶手在作案后几秒钟内即被逮捕，当时一辆流动巡逻警车经过，得以阻止其逃脱。
朱先生刚从办公室出来，穿过河南北路桥，正欲回家时，突然在外滩大楼前，一名独行枪手逼近，开了一枪，子弹击中受害者右太阳穴，随后扔掉武器，试图沿河南北路向北逃跑。此时，附近巡逻的警车抵达现场，追捕枪手，枪手见无路可逃，遂投降。他被带往虹口西区警察局，经讯问后，因调查将在该区域进行，被转移至成都路警察局。

动机不明
谋杀原因仍令警方困惑，因为众所周知朱先生没有任何政治派系关联，尽管昨晚华人圈子指出，他经常刊登读者寄来的反汪精卫文章。

怀疑有政治动机
刑事侦缉处总部和特别分支的侦探也在调查此案，这表明谋杀背后可能有政治动机，但未能获得确切证实。
枪手使用的武器是一把左轮手枪，这表明昨天的暗杀可能与另一名新闻工作者王吉鲁先生（Wang Chi-lu）遇枪击案有关。回想起来，王吉鲁于8月26日上午离开拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette）寓所时遭枪击，据法国警方称，当时也使用了左轮手枪，尽管当时没有逮捕任何枪手。
朱先生谋杀案被移交给成都路警察局，这可能表明他将移交给法国警方进行讯问，因为众所周知，在大多数租界和法租界警力合作的情况下，都是通过成都路警察局进行的。另一方面，移交可能仅仅是为了方便侦探工作。
昨晚有一份可靠但非官方的消息称，昨天被捕的凶手声称自己是游击队员。如果这是真的并得到证实，谋杀案就更加令人费解，因为《大美晚报》的政策是亲华的。另一方面，如果凶手与法租界枪击案有关联，这可能是正确的，因为当时报道称，王先生的报纸刊登了日本人在虹口开办的鱼市场的广告。
据报道，朱先生过去收到过许多恐吓信，最后一封是在周二收到的。
调查正在进行中。

（手写批注：24866 5 9 39）
（手写签名：Liu C 31/8）

SHANGHAI TIMES.
AUG 31 1939
Columnist Of
Ta Mei Wan
Pao Murdered
Victim Shot Dead By
Three Assailants
Near Residence
WAS WELL-KNOWN FOR
PUNGENT ARTICLES
Assassins' guns claimed the
life of another Chinese news-
paperman yesterday afternoon.
Shortly after 4 o'clock, when
Mr. Chu Shing-king, columnist
of the "Ta Mei Wan Pao," the
Chinese edition of the "Shang-
hai Evening Post and Mercury,"
was accosted by three armed
men on North Honan Road,
near Tiendong Road, and shot
dead.
The victim had just left his re-
sidence at No. 94 North Honan Road.
and was proceeding to his office on
Avenue Edward VII. when he was
suddenly attacked by three armed
men, one of whom fired point-blank
at the newspaperman, the bullet
lodging in the left temple and
resulting in instant death.
The shot attracted the attention
of nearby Settlement Chinese police
constables, who rushed to the scene
and succeeded in arresting one of
the assailants, on whose person was
found a revolver and five rounds
of ammunition.
Had Been Threatened
Meanwhile, an ambulance was
called and the victim rushed to the
Lester Chinese Hospital where he
was pronounced dead on arrival.
He was a native of Tanyang, Kiang-
su Province, and was 38 years old.
He had been employed by the "Ta
Mei Wan Pao" since February 1,
1938, and was well-known in Shang-
hai for his pungent articles.
Shortly before the murder, it is
reliably reported, he was the re-
cipient of several threatening
letters.
The dead man is survived by his
wife, nee Miss Ho Li-ying, and a
seven year-old son.
Later in the evening the "Ta Mei
Wan Pao" issued an extra in which
details of the murder were given,
concluding with a statement reiter-
ating the publication's firm intention
of carrying on its newspaper work
without submitting to intimidation
of any sort.

昨日午后，刺客的枪口又夺去了一名中国新闻工作者的生命。下午4时许，《上海晚邮与信使报》中文版《大美晚报》的专栏作家朱惺公先生，在靠近天潼路的北河南路上，遭到三名持械男子拦截并被枪杀身亡。

受害者刚刚离开其位于北河南路94号的住所，正前往爱多亚路（Avenue Edward VII）的报社办公室时，突然遭到三名持械男子的袭击。其中一人近距离向这位新闻工作者开枪，子弹击中左侧太阳穴，导致其当场死亡。

枪声引起了附近租界华捕的注意，他们迅速赶赴现场，并成功逮捕了一名袭击者。在该人身上搜出一支左轮手枪和五发子弹。

曾受威胁

与此同时，当局呼叫了救护车，将受害者紧急送往莱斯德华人医院（Lester Chinese Hospital），但抵达时已被宣告死亡。死者系江苏丹阳人，享年38岁。他自1938年2月1日起受雇于《大美晚报》，因其言辞犀利的文章而在上海广为人知。

据可靠消息，在遇害前不久，他曾收到数封恐吓信。

死者遗孀为何丽英女士（婚前姓何），另有一子，年七岁。

当晚稍后，《大美晚报》发行号外，刊登了谋杀案的详情，并在文末重申该报坚决继续从事新闻工作，绝不屈服于任何形式的恐吓。

SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY.
SEP 2 1939
To Mr. Wang Ching-wei: Where
Do You Stand On Terrorism?
——(An Open Editorial Letter)——
DEAR Mr. Wang Ching-wei:
Over a period of weeks stretching into months we,
and many others in Shanghai as well, have been receiving
anonymous threatening letters from persons or groups
professing allegiance to you. There has been sporadic
violence from these sources. Last Wednesday, August 30,
a member of the staff of our Chinese edition was shot
dead after he had received threats that this would be done
because he did not support your political fortunes.
Law-abiding Chinese and foreigners alike are appalled
at such tactics. You have been subject to the most scath-
ing criticism because of your apparent responsibility for
policies of threat and assassination—the very opposite of
the policies of peace and good order which you have en-
dorsed. Certainly if you have the desire to stand forth as
a man of honesty, sincerity and conscience, you cannot
relish the implication that you are head of a group of
gangster murderers. By no interpretation is it possible
to square such a position with any pretension to lead
reputable elements of the Chinese people.
In this as in all other matters of public interest we
desire to be fair. We do not consider that your partner-
ship with assassination is proved by the mere assertions
of anonymous correspondents. It seems to us that no
man of intelligence, seeking a place of responsibility, can
either inspire or condone such policies of attempted coer-
cion and all too successful violence. We therefore place
before you the choice of pleading “Guilty” by continued
silence, or by giving us a message—which we pledge our-
selves to accord wide publicity—utterly disassociating
yourself from the vermin who have killed Mr. Chu Hsin-
kong and a number of others including one American.
This invitation seems to us a thing which it is de-
cidedly to your advantage to take up. It gives you a
chance to clear your name of the stigma of criminality
and to confine your differences to the sphere of politics.
At the same time, from our own point of view we would
like to see these murderous gangsters shorn of any mantle
of political excuse—if they do not deserve it—and reduced
to the status of ordinary criminals which (if they are
not under your direction) is all they deserve.
In the event that you desire to accept our offer of
an opportunity publicly to clear yourself of the present
sinister implications, the American Editor of the Shang-
hai Evening Post and of the Ta Mei Wan Pao will call
upon you, alone and unarmed, at a time to be fixed by your-
self and under circumstances to be left in your hands.
There are no strings to this offer. No demand is made
that the place of the interview be made known in advance.
Your words will be reported precisely, to any reasonable
length. Our only condition is that we must know, by
first-hand contact, that they come from you.

1939年9月2日
致汪精卫先生：您在恐怖主义问题上持何种立场？
——（一封公开社论信）——

尊敬的汪精卫先生：

在长达数周乃至数月的时间里，我们以及上海的许多其他人一直收到自称效忠于您的个人或团体寄来的匿名恐吓信。来自这些源头的零星暴力事件时有发生。上周三，8月30日，我们中文版的一名员工在收到因不支持您的政治命运而将遭此下场的威胁后，被枪杀身亡。

守法的中国人与外国人均对此类策略感到震惊。由于您似乎对威胁和暗杀政策负有责任——这与您所支持的和平与秩序政策截然相反——您受到了最严厉的批评。当然，如果您希望树立诚实、真诚和有良知的形象，您就不会喜欢被人暗示您是帮派杀手集团的首脑。无论如何解释，都无法将这种立场与领导中国体面人士的企图相调和。

在此事及其他所有公共利益事务上，我们希望保持公平。我们不认为仅凭匿名通信者的断言就能证明您与暗杀行为有合伙关系。在我们看来，任何寻求负责任地位的明智之人，既不会鼓舞也不会纵容此类企图胁迫且往往得逞的暴力政策。因此，我们将以下选择摆在您面前：要么通过继续沉默而 pleading “有罪”，要么给我们一条信息——我们保证予以广泛公开——彻底将自己与杀害朱惺公（Chu Hsin-kong）及其他包括一名美国人在内的多名受害者的害虫划清界限。

在我们看来，接受这一邀请对您显然有利。这使您有机会洗清犯罪污名，并将分歧限制在政治领域。同时，从我们自己的角度来看，我们希望看到这些杀人帮派分子被剥去任何政治借口的伪装（如果他们不配享有这种借口），并沦为普通罪犯的地位，而这（如果他们不受您指挥）正是他们应得的。

如果您希望接受我们提供的公开澄清当前险恶暗示的机会，《上海晚邮报》和《大美晚报》的美籍编辑将单独且不带武器拜访您，时间由您确定，情况由您安排。此提议没有任何附加条件。我们不要求提前告知采访地点。您的话语将被精确报道，篇幅合理。我们唯一的条件是，我们必须通过直接接触确知这些话出自您口。

The "Central China Daily News" publishes

"Your esteemed letter dated August 31,

"Mr. Wang Ching-wei knows nothing about
this affair or about Tsu Sing-kung (朱惺公). However,
a study of Tsu's written works will convince anybody
that he was a communist writer. Taking advantage of his
position on a foreign-owned newspaper, he was engaged
in the dissemination of malicious propaganda against the
real interests of China. Though Mr. Wang Ching-wei
considers that there is absolutely no necessity to pay
any heed to such malicious and defamatory communist
propaganda, yet he is surprised at the failure of your
esteemed paper to observe, so far as the position of your
paper is concerned, the principle that foreigners or
Chinese in foreign employ should maintain a strictly
neutral and impartial attitude and should refrain from
making reckless comments on the internal politics of the
country in which they are residing.
"Political terrorism was started by the
Chungking authorities. During recent months, inhuman
and barbarous acts of this nature have been employed
more vigorously as a weapon to remove persons who are
opposed to them. I was the first one to sustain serious
injuries; this was followed by the fatal wounding of
Dr. Tseng Chung-min (曾仲鳴). Mr. Wang Ching-wei was
very fortunate to have escaped death. According to the
investigations made by the French authorities, the
assassins in the fatal attack on Tseng Chung-min were

“阁下8月31日致李先生（Li）和石先生（Shih）的尊函已收悉。奉命回复如下：-

汪精卫先生对此事及朱惺公（Tsu Sing-kung）一无所知。然而，研读朱氏著作即可使任何人确信，他是一名共产党作家。他利用在外资报社任职的地位，从事散布损害中国真正利益的恶意宣传。虽然汪精卫先生认为完全无需理会此类恶毒且诽谤性的共产党宣传，但他对贵报未能恪守原则感到惊讶。就贵报立场而言，外籍人士或受雇于外人的华人应保持严格的中立和不偏不倚的态度，并避免对其居住国的内政发表鲁莽评论。

政治恐怖主义始于重庆当局。近几个月来，此类非人道和野蛮的行径被更猛烈地用作清除反对者的武器。我是第一个受重伤的人；随后是曾仲鸣（Tseng Chung-min）博士受致命伤。汪精卫先生幸免于难，实属万幸。根据法国当局的调查，在袭击曾仲鸣致死案中的刺客实际上直接受命于重庆的特务机关，其中一些人甚至持有由西南运输公司高官申请签发的香港护照。

该公司是重庆特务机关的大本营之一。沈次高（Sung Tse-kao）先生也在几天前成为卑鄙手段的受害者。在上海，此类活动更为肆无忌惮。然而，贵报对这些暴行未发出任何谴责之声。我难以相信有关贵包庇重庆政府暴行的指控。

收到威胁信的并非只有贵报编辑。我本人以及《华中日报》上海编辑和《华南日报》香港编辑的生命时刻处于危险之中。我们反对利用恐怖活动作为

Translation

Dear Mr. Ts Soong Loo,

We beg to inform you that the attitude of your press, regarding the peaceful movements of Chief Minister Wang, published a lot of nonsensical literature, further owing to the insulting language used, we regret this matter.

Regarding Mr. Wang's great personality and his painful feeling of saving the country and the Koumingtang, all of our countrymen soul favour him. I know you, understand very well that the only people was do not agree with Mr. Wang's attitude are the Chinese Communists, as they have their own secret plan to harm the country. They use their power to break it and the Chungking Government, who are under the authority of the communists.

In future, the part under your editorial, we hope you will keep justice. Not to be utilized by the communists. This is for the good sake of our country and people. Mr. Wang's suggestion, (Anti-Communist) and peaceful movements of saving the country, he does with best determination. He, Mr. Wang, does not wish to follow the terroristic methods which are used by the Chungking Government and he takes no notice of the persons who insult him.

Owing to orders received, that we should carry out the work carefully, we do not use violence against anybody. Ignorant people make a great mistake and think that we are unable to do anything.

From this date, the part under your editorial should be published no more, also the literature or news regarding the Anti-Wang, pro-Communist, or against the peaceful movement. No matter whether it is a Central News Agency's proof or not. Otherwise you are wilfully assisting communism with the intention to turn over to the Koumingtang and harm the country. We will give you no excuse in according to the government's law and warn or notice you no more regarding the above, we will immediately send our men to execute your death sentence, which will give a caution to the others.

After you receive this letter, whether you agree or not, which will be decided upon your own decision.

(Chopped) The Chief Director of the
Communists Extermination and
Save the Country's Bureau.
The Chinese Koumingtang.

译文

亲爱的朱松庐先生：

我们要通知你，你的报界对于汪主席和平运动的态度，发表了许多荒谬的文字，加之使用了侮辱性语言，我们对此事感到遗憾。

关于汪先生的伟大人格及其救国和国民党的痛苦感受，我国同胞的灵魂都拥护他。我知道，你很清楚，唯一不同意汪先生态度的人是中国共产党人，因为他们有自己的秘密计划来危害国家。他们利用自己的力量来破坏它，而重庆政府是在共产党人的权威之下。

今后，在你编辑的部分，我们希望你能保持公正。不要被共产党人利用。这是为了我们国家和人民的利益。汪先生的建议，（反共）和救国的和平运动，他是怀着最大的决心去做的。汪先生不希望遵循重庆政府使用的恐怖主义方法，他也不理会那些侮辱他的人。

由于接到命令，我们要仔细开展工作，我们不使用暴力对付任何人。无知的人犯了一个大错误，认为我们无能为力。

从今天起，你编辑的部分不应再发表，也不应发表有关反汪、亲共或反对和平运动的文字或新闻。无论是否为中央通讯社的证明。否则，你就是故意协助共产主义，意图颠覆国民党并危害国家。根据政府法律，我们将不给你任何借口，也不再就上述事项向你发出警告或通知，我们将立即派人执行对你的死刑判决，以警示他人。

收到此信后，无论你是否同意，将由你自己决定。

（盖章）中国国民党

Road and N.Honan Road corner, I heard a pistol shot the sound
coming from the South.
I drew my pistol and proceeded south on N.Honan Road
and arrested a man running North. At this point station
chauffeur No.38 who was driving motor car No. 110 drew up and
told me that the man I had arrested was not the culprit who
had fired the shot, so I released this man. He then pointed
to one in black clothing who was running West on Tiendong Road
and he also said that he was the murderer who had fired the
shot. I immediately chased and challenged the man and told
him to stop, failing which I would shoot, so the black clothing
man stopped. I arrested him/ I then put the arrested man in
the car and took him to the station. This is my true state-
ment.

At 4.10 p.m. 30-8-39 while driving West Hongkew Station
motor car No. 110 north along North Honan Road near Tiendong
Road I heard a shot fired, the sound came from the East side
of N. Honan Road in front of my car. I immediately looked in
the direction of the sound and saw a male Chinese in the act
of falling to the ground and a second Chinese throw something
on the ground and run in a Northerly direction, I slowed down
my car, and drove behind the man keeping him in view all the
time, the man then turned East into Tiendong Road I stopped
my car at the corner of Tiendong Road and called C.P.C. 164
telling him to arrest the man whom I pointed to, the C.P.C.
arrested one man but I told him he had the wrong man and
pointed to the man I had followed who by that time had turned
round and was running to the west. The C.P.C. then drew his
pistol and challenged the man, who immediately raised his
hands in surrender. I then told the C.P.C. that the arrested
man had shot a male Chinese on N. Honan Road.
We then entered the car and came to the station.

(signed by Chauffeur Tsung Ping Tau)
(签名)
